title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Fix a set L, finite in practice. A 'multiplicity' (multiplicité, also called a figure) is an admissible family X of subsets of L, so X ⊂ 𝔓(L). The admissibility axioms come from the preceding pages and are only partly visible here. One of them is that every A in the family has nonempty interior A°, so in particular ∅ ∉ X. The family {∅} is therefore not admissible.

M is the poset of all multiplicities. The order comes from page 11: F ≤ G means F is a 'restriction' of G of the kind G_A = {Y ∈ G | Y ⊆ A}. Two elements are compatible if they have a common upper bound. Earlier axioms (C1–C4) describe a general 'algebra of figures' as a poset that decomposes into connected components. This page and the next check that, in the model 'families of subsets of L', this decomposition is trivial: M is connected.

Argument on this page.
(1) The minimal elements of M are the singletons {A} with A ≠ ∅. Indeed 𝔏_A = {A} whenever A ∈ 𝔏, and A ∈ 𝔏 forces A° ≠ ∅, hence A ≠ ∅.
(2) Suppose X ∈ M has a minimal element A (for example, X finite). Then X_A = {A} ≤ X, so X and {A} lie in the same connected component.
(3) Suppose A ≠ L and x ∈ L∖A. Then {A} and {{x}} lie in the same component, since both are majorised by the multiplicity {A, {x}, A∪{x}}. Grothendieck writes this sloppily as {{A},{{x}},A∪{{x}}}.
(4) For x, y ∈ L, the singletons {{x}} and {{y}} lie in one component. Hence every X with a minimal element A ≠ L lies in the component of the points.
(5) The remaining case is X = {L}. The next page links {L} to {{x}} via a multiplicity built from {x} and L∖{x}.
(6) Degenerate cases (next page). If L = ∅ then M = ∅. If card L = 1 then M = {{L}}.

Conclusion. Restricting to finite multiplicities, M is connected. The axiom C4 (decomposition into connected components, with comparability inside components) is then automatic in this model. The page is a routine verification inside Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'figures'.
errors: The majorant is written {{A},{{x}},A∪{{x}}}, mixing levels of braces; it should be the family {A, {x}, A∪{x}}. Moreover, the next page's join of {L} with {{x}} via {{x},{L∖{x}}} does not obviously majorise {L} unless L itself is included (or the order is not mere restriction). The text is sloppy at this point.

Step (2) needs X to have a minimal element. The finiteness assumption is acknowledged ('p.ex. X fini'), and the conclusion is correctly restricted to finite multiplicities on the next page. For infinite X with no minimal element, connectedness is left open.
That 'X_A ≤ X' and 'majorised by' behave as claimed depends on the precise definition of ≤ (sieve/restriction order) and of admissibility, which are given on earlier pages and not fully visible here.

ideas.what: Minimal elements of the poset of admissible set-families are the singleton families {A}, A ≠ ∅
ideas.modern_name: atoms/minimal elements of a poset of set systems (sieve-type order)

ideas.what: Connectedness of the poset M of multiplicities, via common upper bounds such as {A, {x}, A∪{x}}
ideas.modern_name: connectedness of a poset / comparability graph

ideas.what: Checking that axiom C4 (decomposition into connected components) is automatic in the model 'admissible families of subsets of L'
ideas.modern_name: model verification of an axiomatic 'algebra of figures' (close in spirit to abstract cell complexes / combinatorial tame topology)
ideas.where_published: The general 'géométrie modérée' programme appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this specific axiomatics is unpublished as far as known.

missed.claim: The connectedness of M is established only for finite multiplicities (or those with minimal elements). The infinite case, and the role of the admissibility condition A° ≠ ∅ (a topological constraint), are left open.
missed.quote: si X admet un élément minimal A (p.ex. X fini)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of minor interest. It documents that the 1986 'Algèbre des figures' axioms were tested against concrete set-system models. That bears on reconstructing his late tame-topology programme, but the content itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary poset-connectedness verification within an unpublished axiomatic framework. Historically mildly interesting as part of the 1986 'figures' project, but there is no substantive new mathematics on the page.
transcription_corrections: 'ens des multi-sets[?]' is more plausibly 'ens. des multiplicités' (the word is broken across lines: 'multi-' / '...tés').
'A ∈ L ⇒ A° ≠ ∅' should read 'A ∈ 𝔏 ⇒ A° ≠ ∅ a fortiori A ≠ ∅'.
The majorant should be read as the family {A, {x}, A∪{x}}; the manuscript writes '{{A},{{x}}, A∪{{x}}}'.
'Et pour C = vaut' is uncertain; it is probably 'Et par C = connexe ... les {{x}} pour tous les élts de L sont dans la même comp. connexe'.
The last line ends with 'si [Card] L ≠ ∅' with crossings; the intended condition concerns L having at least two elements, so that x and L∖{x} are both nonempty.
